title: Grind peppercorns in a marble mortar: hold the mortar still by a lug while the other hand grinds with the pestle
instruction: Grind the peppercorns in the marble mortar to powder: hold the mortar still by one of its lugs with one hand, and with the other take the wooden pestle and grind round and round on the bottom of the bowl until every peppercorn is ground. Then stand the pestle back up on its tea towel and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Grinding spices in a mortar is an everyday kitchen job that people with the use of only one hand cannot do: on a smooth worktop the mortar slides and turns with the pestle unless the other hand holds it.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A polished black granite kitchen worktop 1 cm thick, from 16 to 48 cm forward and from 26.5 cm right to 20 cm left of the centre line, fixed. (2) A white Carrara marble mortar (0.45 kg), its middle 33 cm forward and 5 cm right of the centre line: 15.6 cm across and 5.5 cm tall, its bowl 11.6 cm across and 4 cm deep, with four rounded lugs (2.4 cm wide, 2 cm thick) at its rim pointing front-left, back-left, back-right and front-right. (3) In the bowl, a small heap of twelve black peppercorns (7 mm). (4) A beech pestle (0.12 kg) 11 cm long, its head 3.8 cm across and its handle 2.3 cm across, standing on its broad end on (5) a folded cream linen tea towel with two red stripes, 10 x 10 cm, its middle 29 cm forward and 20 cm right of the centre line, fixed. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Grinding is a rule: while the pestle's end is on the bowl's floor (within 8 mm of it, the pestle within 35 degrees of upright) and the mortar moved less than 1.5 mm and turned less than 0.75 degrees in that control step, the distance the pestle's end moves across the floor counts as rubbing. Every 9.4 cm of rubbing (one round 3 cm across) grinds a fifth of the peppercorns: fewer peppercorns and more powder show in the bowl. 1.0: every peppercorn ground (five rounds' worth), the pestle standing on its tea towel (upright within 20 degrees, its broad end within 4.5 cm of the towel's middle and resting on it), the mortar upright (under 10 degrees) on the worktop, and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: every peppercorn ground; 0.25: at least two rounds' worth ground; else 0.0. Judged at the end of the trial, which ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the mortar and the pestle still.
reset_notes: Stand the pestle back on its tea towel and put the mortar back in its place; the peppercorns reappear at every reset.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: grinding is a rule (see scoring); the peppercorns and the powder are drawn shapes that do not collide. The mortar weighs 0.45 kg (a real one about 2 kg), and the polished worktop has a friction of 0.1, so a pestle pressed on the bowl's floor drags an unheld mortar. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
